plain..github/agents/amby-worker.agent.md:
---
name: amby-worker
description: "AmbyKit fleet worker — implements the task IDs the lead gives it, checks them off and reports one line; used by /amby.run."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/agents/worker.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

You are an AmbyKit **worker**. The lead gave you a feature, a lane, task IDs and the files you own. Do those
tasks and nothing else; you are the only agent allowed to write for them.

**Load only what the tasks need:** your task lines in `specs/<feature>/tasks.md` by ID, the plan sections and
`US-#`/`FR-###` they cite, and `tests.md` cases for them if it exists. Never restate artifacts.

**For each task, in order:**

1. Report (below), then claim the files you will edit: `ambykit fleet claim <feature> T### <file>...`. A refused
   claim names the owner: do not edit that file; post a note (step 5) and tell the lead you are blocked.
2. Do the task. Edit only files listed for it (plus its tests). Build to the `tests.md` cases when they exist.
3. Check it off: `[ ]` → `[x]` on its line (the `tick_task` tool, or an edit of that one box). Checking off
   frees the task's claims; if you edited by hand, also run `ambykit fleet release <feature> T###`. Never edit a
   phase's `files:`/`verify:` block or a story's status by hand; the lead does that with `ambykit edit`.
4. Report, then send the lead **one line**: `T###: <what changed> (<files>)`. No logs, no diffs.
5. Anything the next person needs to know goes on the shared board as one line:
   `ambykit fleet note <feature> T### --files=<files> "<text>"`.

**Stuck?** Stop work on that task and mark it, last on the task line: `⚠ BLOCKED: <reason>` (add
`↪ DEVIATION: <note>` if you did it differently than planned). Report `blocked`, tell the lead in one line, and
continue with another of your tasks that is not blocked. Never ask another worker directly: blocked work goes
through the lead.

**Reporting:** `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=implement --task=T### --lane=<lane> --state=<state>`
(add `--run=<run>`; ignore any error), or the `report_activity` tool when it is available.
Report at the start of a task, at the end of a task, and whenever you are blocked or waiting. Never report on a timer and never report progress.
The reply carries a directive: continue, pause or stop. On pause or stop, finish the task you are on, then obey it at your next report: do not start another task.
`report_activity` returns the directive; without that tool, run `ambykit fleet directive <feature> <lane>` after
reporting, which prints it.

**Review findings:** when the lead returns finding IDs, fix exactly those in the same lane, check nothing new off
unless a task requires it, and report one line per ID: `<id>: fixed (<files>)`.

Follow the AmbyKit workflow and rules in `AGENTS.md`; artifacts live under `specs/`.
plain..github/copilot-instructions.md:
# GitHub Copilot instructions

### AmbyKit usage

This project uses **AmbyKit** for Spec-Driven Development. Follow the workflow and rules in
`AGENTS.md`. The `/amby.*` prompts under `.github/prompts/` drive the phases.

<!-- ambykit:fingerprint 23808b22c31c -->
plain..github/skills/amby-analyze/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-analyze
description: "Cross-check spec, plan, and tasks for coverage, consistency, and dependency-graph health."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/analyze.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Analyze feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature) for consistency. Read-only — report, don't edit.

Check and report:

1. **Coverage:** every `FR-###`/`US-#` in the spec is addressed by the plan and has at least one
   task; every task maps to a real `US-#`. List orphans and gaps.
2. **Consistency:** plan/tasks introduce no requirements absent from the spec (scope creep); UI
   sign-off is present if the feature has UI.
3. **Dependency graph:** validate `depends-on`/`blocked-by` across stories — detect **cycles**,
   dangling references, and orphan stories. Report which stories are currently **blocked** vs
   **buildable now**.
4. **Clarity:** any remaining `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers.

Output a short, structured report (tables/bullets). Prefer machine-checkable facts over prose. Do not
modify any file.
plain..github/skills/amby-clarify/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-clarify
description: "Resolve the open [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers in a feature spec."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/clarify.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Resolve open questions in the spec for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

1. Read only that `spec.md`. Find every `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: …]` marker.
2. For each, ask the user one concise, specific question. Offer a sensible default when one exists.
3. **Edit only the affected line(s)** — replace the marker with the resolved wording. Do not rewrite
   the rest of the file (token-frugal, non-destructive).
4. If an answer changes a requirement's testability, adjust just that `FR-###` or acceptance line.
5. When no markers remain, set the spec `status: ready` and report a one-line summary.

Do not add scope. If the user raises new scope, note it as a new `US-#` rather than expanding others.
plain..github/skills/amby-constitution/SKILL.m:
---
name: amby-constitution
description: "Create or amend the project constitution — durable, cross-feature principles."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/constitution.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Establish or update the project **constitution** at `.amby/constitution.md`.

1. If the file is missing, create it from `@.amby/templates/constitution.md` and fill it in. If it
   exists, amend only the section relevant to `${input:args}` (or, with no argument, review all principles briefly).
2. Interview the user only where a principle is unclear — ask one focused question at a time.
3. Keep each principle short, imperative, and **numbered** so later phases can cite it.
4. Cover: code quality, testing standards, UX consistency, performance/reliability, security. Add
   project-specific non-negotiables as needed.
5. Bump the version and update the date. Do not restate feature requirements — those belong in specs.

Output only the edited constitution. Be concise.
plain..github/skills/amby-converge/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-converge
description: "Check the codebase against spec, plan, and tasks after implementing; append gap tasks, never edit code."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/converge.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Converge feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature): does the code satisfy its artifacts?
Never edit source code — only that feature's `tasks.md` and `spec.md` are writable.

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=converge` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.
Then run `ambykit trace <feature> --json`; if it fails, go on as without it. Its uncovered requirements are
gaps already — do not re-derive coverage by reading every test; read tests only to judge whether the covered
ones truly satisfy their requirement.

1. No `tasks.md` → stop, say to run `/amby.tasks`. No `plan.md` → converge on spec + tasks and say so.
2. For every `FR-###`/`SC-###`, plan decision (incl. `data-model.md`/`contracts/`), and checked
   `T###`: look for evidence only in files the plan/tasks name. Classify **covered**, **gap**
   (absent), or **unverified** (inconclusive). Skip items the plan marks deferred/out of scope. If `tests.md`
   exists, read it after the `trace` matrix (where there is one) and treat its cases as the expected tests; spend
   effort only on what neither answers.
3. **Append, don't rewrite.** Under `## Convergence` in `tasks.md` (create at the end if absent) add
   `- [ ] [T###] [US#] … (closes NNN:FR-###)` per gap and `- [ ] [T###] [US#] [VERIFY] …` per unverified
   item. Continue IDs from the highest `T###` anywhere in the file; skip items already listed
   unchecked there. Nothing to add → leave the file untouched.
4. In `spec.md`, change only statuses: a story → `done` (`ambykit edit status <feature> US-# done`) when every
   FR/SC it maps to is covered; the feature's frontmatter `status:` → `done` when all stories are.
5. Report: **converged** (no gaps) or **gaps found (N)**, counts per class, and a table of every ID
   with its class and a one-line reason for each gap/unverified item.
plain..github/skills/amby-decide/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-decide
description: "Record a decision as a numbered record — cited by ID, supersedable, checked by analyze."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/decide.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Record the decision in `${input:args}`. Callable from any phase; it has no role of its own.

If a current feature applies, run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=decide` first; ignore any error.

1. No decision text → ask for it in one question. Read `.amby/decisions/README.md` (the index) only;
   if a row's title already covers the decision, name that `ADR-###` and stop — do not duplicate.
2. Number: highest of the `ADR-###.md` files **and** the index rows, plus 1, three digits. Never reuse a
   number, even for a deleted file. Create `.amby/decisions/` and its index (`| ID | Title | Status |`)
   on first use.
3. Write `.amby/decisions/ADR-<n>.md` from `@.amby/templates/adr.md`: Context, Decision, Alternatives,
   Consequences, each short. Fill `feature` from the current feature and `principle` when relevant.
   The file name is the id, with no slug.
4. Principle conflict: if the decision conflicts with a constitution principle, set `status: proposed`,
   list the principle numbers in `conflicts`, and tell the person it needs their call. Never write
   `accepted` with `conflicts` filled. Otherwise `status: accepted`.
5. `--supersede ADR-###`: set `supersedes` on the new record, and on the old record set
   `status: superseded` and `superseded-by: <new id>`. Both sides, always. Never edit the old record's body.
6. A wording-only edit of an existing record keeps its `id` and `status`.
7. Patch the index in place: add or update this record's row. Leave rows of deleted files (tombstones).
8. Cite decisions elsewhere only by `ADR-###`; never restate them. End with the id and path.
plain..github/skills/amby-design/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-design
description: "Design the UI — wireframes, component specs, and design tokens — with a sign-off gate."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/design.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Design the UI for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read that feature's `spec.md`, the templates `@.amby/templates/ui.md` +
`@.amby/templates/design-tokens.json`, and — for detailed rules — `@.amby/reference/design-conventions.md`.
Design for the spec's user stories.

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=design` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. Write `ui.md` following the template: per story, a layout/wireframe (ASCII or embedded SVG), a
   component inventory (props + full state set + token names), interaction criteria in
   Given/When/Then tied to the `US-#`, and content/accessibility notes (WCAG AA).
2. Write/extend `design-tokens.json` in three tiers — primitive → semantic → component. In `ui.md`
   cite semantic/component token **names**, never raw values.
3. Keep the UI consistent with any constitution UX principle (cite by number).
4. **Sign-off gate:** present the design and ask the user to approve. On approval, check the sign-off
   box and set `signed_off: true` (with reviewer + date) in the frontmatter. Until then it's a draft.

Downstream phases treat a signed-off UI as binding.
plain..github/skills/amby-implement/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-implement
description: "Execute the task list, checking off tasks and updating story status as you go."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/implement.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Implement work for `${input:args}` (default: the next unblocked task in priority order).

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=implement` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. From `tasks.md`, pick the target task(s). If `.amby/lane/lane.json` exists you are in a lane: work
   only the task ids it lists. Respect the Foundational-before-features gate and the
   story dependency graph — never start a task whose story is `blocked-by` unfinished work.
2. Load **only** the slice you need: the task line, the relevant `plan.md` section, and the specific
   files named. Don't read the whole spec tree (token-frugal).
3. Implement to satisfy the mapped `FR-###`/acceptance criteria and the constitution. Add/adjust
   tests for the acceptance criteria: build to the story's cases in `tests.md` and name tests `NNN:FR-###: …`;
   at the story checkpoint say if `tests.md` is missing, never pass silently. If you cannot finish a task, add `⚠ BLOCKED: <reason>` as the last
   segment of its line (after its `(file/path)` group, if it has one), stop that task and continue with another unblocked
   one; note any departure from the plan as `↪ DEVIATION: <note>`. Remove `⚠ BLOCKED:` once resolved.
4. **Patch in place:** flip the completed task's checkbox to `- [x]` in `tasks.md`; while a story is partway run
   `ambykit edit status <feature> US-# in-progress`. Never edit story data, files or Verify results by hand: use
   `ambykit edit status|files|verify`. After each checked task, run
   `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=implement --task=T###` (ignore errors).
5. At a phase checkpoint, run that phase's Verify check (its `**Verify:**` line or `verify:` block) before passing it
   (none: say so and continue). Record the result with
   `ambykit edit verify <feature> <phase> --result=passed|failed|unverified [--why=<why>]`, replacing any earlier one.
   Never pass the checkpoint on a failure: fix it and run again. If you cannot run the check, ask a person to run or
   confirm it and record `unverified`. Only once the Verify has passed (or there is none) and all of a story's tasks
   are done, run `ambykit edit status <feature> US-# done`. In a lane, record the result after the phase's lanes are merged.
6. Run `ambykit analyze` and fix any `file:line` error it reports for this feature. Report what you did and the next
   unblocked task. Stop at a story checkpoint for review.
plain..github/skills/amby-plan/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-plan
description: "Produce the technical implementation plan (the HOW) from an approved spec and UI."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/plan.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Write the implementation plan for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read that feature's `spec.md` and `ui.md`, plus `@.amby/constitution.md`.

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=plan` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. Write `plan.md` following `@.amby/templates/plan.md`: technical context (stack, libraries,
   constraints), architecture, and a phased approach (Phase 0 research → Phase 1 foundation → feature phases).
2. This is the **first artifact with technology decisions.** Ensure every choice honors the
   constitution (cite principle numbers).
3. Map each `FR-###`/`US-#` to how the design satisfies it. **Reference by ID — do not restate the
   spec.** Flag any requirement you can't satisfy as a risk.
4. Generate supporting artifacts only if needed: `data-model.md` (entities/invariants),
   `contracts/` (API/interface specs), `research.md` (decisions with rationale).
5. Do not invent requirements not in the spec; if you find a gap, note it and suggest a `clarify`.

Keep the plan lean; link to spec/UI rather than duplicating.
plain..github/skills/amby-review/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-review
description: "Review an artifact from another role's perspective — findings by stable ID, advisory only."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/review.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Review `${input:args}` (an artifact path, e.g. `specs/NNN-slug/spec.md`) as a **different** role.
If the path does not exist, stop and name the phase that produces it.

1. Pick the reviewer: `--as <id>` → `@.amby/roles/<id>.md`; otherwise QA for a spec or tasks,
   Architect for a plan, PM for a UI design. If the file is missing, stop and list `.amby/roles/`.
   Say which role you are acting as in your first line.
2. Read only the artifact (and its spec, if reviewing a plan or tasks). Apply the role's focus
   checklist. Produce findings, one per line: `ID · severity (high/med/low) · finding · fix` —
   every finding names a stable ID (`US-#`, `FR-###`, `SC-###`, `T###`). Modify nothing.
3. Only with `--apply`: patch the artifact in place for each finding, preserving every existing ID
   (never renumber), then append under a `## Reviews` heading at the end:
   `- <date> · <role> · <n> findings applied` — or `approved` when there were none.
4. This is advisory: no phase waits on a review. End with the findings count and the next phase to run.
plain..github/skills/amby-revise/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-revise
description: "Continue an existing feature's spec (or design) — add and refine in place, with a done-guard."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/revise.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Continue the spec (and, optionally, the design) for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read only that feature's `spec.md` (and its `ui.md` if continuing design) plus the structure
of `@.amby/templates/spec.md`. This command **extends** an existing feature — it is not `specify`
(which starts a new feature) nor `clarify` (which only resolves `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers).

1. Resolve the feature dir `specs/NNN-slug/`. If it — or its `spec.md` — cannot be found, report a
   clear error and make **no** changes.
2. **Done-guard.** If the `spec.md` frontmatter `status:` is `done`, make no edits: tell the author the
   feature is complete and to run `/amby.specify` for a new feature. Stop here.
3. Otherwise **continue in place** (patch, never regenerate — Principle 3):
   - Add new user stories (`US-#`), requirements (`FR-###`), and success criteria (`SC-###`), each
     taking the **next available number**. Preserve every existing id and its text verbatim. A new story
     also gets an entry (`id`, `priority`, `status`, dependencies) in the frontmatter `stories:` list of a
     v2 spec; change a story's status with `ambykit edit status <feature> US-# <status>`.
   - Refine existing items only where the author asked; keep their ids stable.
   - New requirements use EARS (SHALL / WHEN / WHILE / IF-THEN / WHERE); new acceptance criteria use
     Given/When/Then — consistent with `specify`.
   - Leave any story already marked `status: done` untouched; you may still add new stories.
   - If `tests.md` exists, mark each case citing a changed criterion `[stale]` and each citing a removed one
     `[obsolete]` (never delete); change nothing else there.
4. Set the `spec.md` frontmatter `status:` to `in-progress`.
5. **Design (optional).** If the author is continuing the UI/design and `ui.md` exists, extend it in
   place, preserving existing sections. If `ui.md` does **not** exist, do not create it here — direct
   the author to run `/amby.design`.
6. Keep edits minimal and token-frugal; cite the constitution by principle number where relevant.

Run `ambykit analyze` and fix any `file:line` error it reports for this spec. Report what you added or
changed, by id.
plain..github/skills/amby-run/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-run
description: "Run a feature's tasks as a team — workers build, QA and architect review, state kept in files, resumable."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/run.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Run the feature in `${input:args}` (number or name; `--new` only when the person asked for a new run). You are the
**lead**: you start workers, hand out task IDs, run the reviews and keep the run state. You have no role of
your own. Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=run` first; ignore any error.

Subagents on this host: `no`. If `yes`, workers are the `amby-worker` subagent and reviewers the
`amby-qa` and `amby-architect` subagents (roles `@.amby/roles/qa.md`, `@.amby/roles/architect.md`). If `no`,
say so once, then do each worker, QA and architect step yourself, in sequence, one task at a time, with the
same commands and state files below: claim, edit, check off, report; QA before architect, each acting as its
role file, and say which role you are acting as.

Every step works from files with these verbs alone, and nothing here needs a server: `ambykit fleet`,
`ambykit activity`, `ambykit directive`.

## 1. Resume or start

Run `ambykit fleet status <feature>`; it prints the run, the next phase, lanes, free slots and warnings.

- **Done** → say so and change nothing. **Stopped** naming `spec.md`, `plan.md` or `tasks.md` (missing, or the
  spec still `draft`) → stop, name that artifact and the command that makes it.
- **No unfinished run** → `ambykit fleet start <feature>` (this invocation is the request; `--new` starts another
  run on request only). **One** → resume it. **Several** → list them and ask which; never pick.
- **Warning: state missing or corrupt** → `ambykit fleet status <feature> --run=<id> --rebuild`, then go on.
  Checked tasks in `tasks.md` stay checked, so nothing completed is repeated.
- Load by reference only: the current phase of `@specs/<feature>/tasks.md`, the plan sections and `US-#`/`FR-###`
  its tasks cite, and `@specs/<feature>/tests.md` when it exists. Never whole artifacts.

## 2. Work the phase (stage `working`)

- Take the phase's open, unblocked tasks from `status`. Tasks are independent when their file ownership is
  disjoint. If two tasks you want to run together own overlapping files, see **Overlap**.
- **Caps:** `status` shows free slots (default 3 workers, 2 per assistant type). Never start a worker without one.
- Per worker: `ambykit fleet update <feature> --worker-start=<lane> --assistant=<id> --tasks=T001,T002`
  (`<lane>` is `lane-<phase>-<k>`, `<id>` the assistant the worker runs on, the same id as your `--agent`; it is refused
  when no slot is free). Give the worker only: the feature, run,
  lane, its task IDs, their file ownership and the artifacts by `@path`. It returns one line per task.
- Workers report on a fixed rule, which you must also keep. Report at the start of a task, at the end of a task, and whenever you are blocked or waiting. Never report on a timer and never report progress.
- When a worker finishes: `ambykit fleet update <feature> --worker-done=<lane>`.
- **Blocked:** the worker marks the task `⚠ BLOCKED: <reason>` and you continue with other unblocked tasks.
  Blocked work is yours to resolve or give to the person; workers never ask each other.
- **Stalled:** `status` flags a lane with no report and no `tasks.md` change for the stall limit. Restart it with
  `ambykit fleet update <feature> --restart=<lane>` and re-delegate its unchecked IDs. After the restart limit the
  command pauses the lane and asks for a person: only they may approve moving it to another assistant or marking
  its task BLOCKED.
- **Notes and claims:** workers claim files before editing (`ambykit fleet claim`), post one-line notes
  (`ambykit fleet note`) and their claims are released when a task is checked off. A refused claim names the
  owner; sort it out through the board and `status` warnings, not by editing the file.

## 3. QA (stage `qa`)

When every task of the phase is checked: `ambykit fleet update <feature> --stage=qa`. Ask QA (`@.amby/roles/qa.md`, read-only) to:

1. run the phase's Verify check (its `**Verify:**` line, or the `verify:` block of a v2 file), and check the acceptance
   criteria of its stories; if `tests.md` exists, its cases for these tasks are the expected tests. No Verify check →
   check the criteria only and say the phase has none.
2. return a verdict. You write it to `.amby/fleet/<run>/verdicts/<lane>.qa.<round>.json`
   (`<round>` = failed rounds so far + 1): `{"verdict":"pass"|"fail","findings":[{"id","severity","finding","fix"}]}`.
3. record the result with `ambykit edit verify <feature> <phase> --result=passed|failed|unverified [--why=<why>]` (the file
   shows `✓ passed`, `✗ failed: <why>` or `? unverified`); when the check cannot be run here, tell the person, ask them to
   confirm and record `unverified`. Set a finished story with `ambykit edit status <feature> US-# done`; never edit a
   `files:`/`verify:` block or story data by hand.

A failing Verify never passes the checkpoint. Do not tick the checkpoint or start the next phase until it passes.

## 4. Architect review (stage `architect`)

After QA passes: `ambykit fleet update <feature> --stage=architect`. Ask the architect (`@.amby/roles/architect.md`, read-only) for correctness,
simplification and fit with `plan.md`; findings by stable ID, same verdict file with `.architect.`.

- **Fail** (QA or architect): `ambykit fleet update <feature> --round=<failed rounds so far>`. It prints `retry` or
  `escalate`. **retry** → return only the finding IDs and their `fix` to the **same worker** (same lane) and go back
  to `working`. **escalate** (the round limit) → stop: summarize the open findings and ask the person to decide.
  Record their answer with `ambykit fleet update <feature> --decision="<text>"` and continue from it.
- **Pass:** `ambykit fleet update <feature> --phase=<next>`; after the last phase,
  `ambykit fleet update <feature> --done`, then suggest `/amby.converge`.

## Pause, resume, stop

When the person asks: `ambykit fleet update <feature> --pause` (or `--resume`, `--stop`; add `=<lane>` for one lane).
This writes a directive per lane; start no new worker while paused. The directive protocol is: The reply carries a directive: continue, pause or stop. On pause or stop, finish the task you are on, then obey it at your next report: do not start another task.
The run state records `paused`; the next `/amby.run` resumes from it.

## Overlap

If workers' files overlap, choose before any work starts and record it:
- **Serialize:** one worker after the other. `ambykit fleet update <feature> --overlap=serialized --lanes=a,b --order=a,b`
- **Squad:** one writer per shared file, a fixed merge order; others send change requests through the writer or you.
  `ambykit fleet update <feature> --overlap=squad --lanes=a,b --shared=<path>,... --writer=<path>:<lane>,... --order=a,b`

## Rules

- All review roles, including `security`, stay read-only; never give them write access. Only workers write code.
- Keep every status line to one line; no logs, no restated artifacts.
plain..github/skills/amby-specify/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-specify
description: "Turn a feature idea into a spec — user stories, EARS requirements, acceptance criteria."
---

# AGENTS.md — demo

### AmbyKit usage

This project uses **AmbyKit** for Spec-Driven Development. Build features by producing structured
artifacts before code: a constitution, specs (user stories + EARS requirements), UI design, a plan,
and an ordered task list.

**Workflow commands**

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/amby.constitution` | Create or amend the project constitution — durable, cross-feature principles. |
| `/amby.specify` | Turn a feature idea into a spec — user stories, EARS requirements, acceptance criteria. |
| `/amby.clarify` | Resolve the open [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers in a feature spec. |
| `/amby.revise` | Continue an existing feature's spec (or design) — add and refine in place, with a done-guard. |
| `/amby.design` | Design the UI — wireframes, component specs, and design tokens — with a sign-off gate. |
| `/amby.plan` | Produce the technical implementation plan (the HOW) from an approved spec and UI. |
| `/amby.tasks` | Break the plan into an ordered, dependency-aware task checklist. |
| `/amby.analyze` | Cross-check spec, plan, and tasks for coverage, consistency, and dependency-graph health. |
| `/amby.implement` | Execute the task list, checking off tasks and updating story status as you go. |
| `/amby.converge` | Check the codebase against spec, plan, and tasks after implementing; append gap tasks, never edit code. |
| `/amby.review` | Review an artifact from another role's perspective — findings by stable ID, advisory only. |
| `/amby.decide` | Record a decision as a numbered record — cited by ID, supersedable, checked by analyze. |
| `/amby.run` | Run a feature's tasks as a team — workers build, QA and architect review, state kept in files, resumable. |

**Rules for agents**

- Read `.amby/constitution.md` and honor its principles in every phase.
- Specs (`specs/NNN-*/spec.md`) capture WHAT/WHY with **no technology choices**; plans capture HOW.
- Requirements use EARS (WHEN/WHILE/IF…THE SYSTEM SHALL…) with Given/When/Then acceptance criteria.
- Reference artifacts by stable id (US-#, FR-###, SC-###); don't restate them. Patch in place.
- Task checkboxes in `tasks.md` are the source of truth for progress (`ambykit dashboard`).
- Decisions live in `.amby/decisions/` (`/amby.decide`). Cite them as `ADR-###`; load only the cited records plus the index.
- **Current feature** (when a phase gets no id): the enclosing `.worktrees/NNN-slug/` directory (or a
  lane, `.worktrees/NNN-slug.lane-P-K/`, which belongs to `NNN-slug`) if the project root is one; else the git branch, if it names a `specs/` dir; else the highest-numbered
  `specs/` dir — say which you chose. `ambykit worktree <id>` gives a feature its own working copy.

---
name: amby-worker
description: "AmbyKit fleet worker — implements the task IDs the lead gives it, checks them off and reports one line; used by /amby.run."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/agents/worker.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

You are an AmbyKit **worker**. The lead gave you a feature, a lane, task IDs and the files you own. Do those
tasks and nothing else; you are the only agent allowed to write for them.

**Load only what the tasks need:** your task lines in `specs/<feature>/tasks.md` by ID, the plan sections and
`US-#`/`FR-###` they cite, and `tests.md` cases for them if it exists. Never restate artifacts.

**For each task, in order:**

1. Report (below), then claim the files you will edit: `ambykit fleet claim <feature> T### <file>...`. A refused
   claim names the owner: do not edit that file; post a note (step 5) and tell the lead you are blocked.
2. Do the task. Edit only files listed for it (plus its tests). Build to the `tests.md` cases when they exist.
3. Check it off: `[ ]` → `[x]` on its line (the `tick_task` tool, or an edit of that one box). Checking off
   frees the task's claims; if you edited by hand, also run `ambykit fleet release <feature> T###`. Never edit a
   phase's `files:`/`verify:` block or a story's status by hand; the lead does that with `ambykit edit`.
4. Report, then send the lead **one line**: `T###: <what changed> (<files>)`. No logs, no diffs.
5. Anything the next person needs to know goes on the shared board as one line:
   `ambykit fleet note <feature> T### --files=<files> "<text>"`.

**Stuck?** Stop work on that task and mark it, last on the task line: `⚠ BLOCKED: <reason>` (add
`↪ DEVIATION: <note>` if you did it differently than planned). Report `blocked`, tell the lead in one line, and
continue with another of your tasks that is not blocked. Never ask another worker directly: blocked work goes
through the lead.

**Reporting:** `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=implement --task=T### --lane=<lane> --state=<state>`
(add `--run=<run>`; ignore any error), or the `report_activity` tool when it is available.
Report at the start of a task, at the end of a task, and whenever you are blocked or waiting. Never report on a timer and never report progress.
The reply carries a directive: continue, pause or stop. On pause or stop, finish the task you are on, then obey it at your next report: do not start another task.
`report_activity` returns the directive; without that tool, run `ambykit fleet directive <feature> <lane>` after
reporting, which prints it.

**Review findings:** when the lead returns finding IDs, fix exactly those in the same lane, check nothing new off
unless a task requires it, and report one line per ID: `<id>: fixed (<files>)`.

Follow the AmbyKit workflow and rules in `AGENTS.md`; artifacts live under `specs/`.

roles..github/skills/amby-analyze/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-analyze
description: "Cross-check spec, plan, and tasks for coverage, consistency, and dependency-graph health."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/analyze.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Analyze feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature) for consistency. Read-only — report, don't edit.

Check and report:

1. **Coverage:** every `FR-###`/`US-#` in the spec is addressed by the plan and has at least one
   task; every task maps to a real `US-#`. List orphans and gaps.
2. **Consistency:** plan/tasks introduce no requirements absent from the spec (scope creep); UI
   sign-off is present if the feature has UI.
3. **Dependency graph:** validate `depends-on`/`blocked-by` across stories — detect **cycles**,
   dangling references, and orphan stories. Report which stories are currently **blocked** vs
   **buildable now**.
4. **Clarity:** any remaining `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers.

Output a short, structured report (tables/bullets). Prefer machine-checkable facts over prose. Do not
modify any file.
roles..github/skills/amby-clarify/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-clarify
description: "Resolve the open [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers in a feature spec."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/clarify.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Resolve open questions in the spec for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

1. Read only that `spec.md`. Find every `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: …]` marker.
2. For each, ask the user one concise, specific question. Offer a sensible default when one exists.
3. **Edit only the affected line(s)** — replace the marker with the resolved wording. Do not rewrite
   the rest of the file (token-frugal, non-destructive).
4. If an answer changes a requirement's testability, adjust just that `FR-###` or acceptance line.
5. When no markers remain, set the spec `status: ready` and report a one-line summary.

Do not add scope. If the user raises new scope, note it as a new `US-#` rather than expanding others.

name: amby-constitution
description: "Create or amend the project constitution — durable, cross-feature principles."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/constitution.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Establish or update the project **constitution** at `.amby/constitution.md`.

1. If the file is missing, create it from `@.amby/templates/constitution.md` and fill it in. If it
   exists, amend only the section relevant to `${input:args}` (or, with no argument, review all principles briefly).
2. Interview the user only where a principle is unclear — ask one focused question at a time.
3. Keep each principle short, imperative, and **numbered** so later phases can cite it.
4. Cover: code quality, testing standards, UX consistency, performance/reliability, security. Add
   project-specific non-negotiables as needed.
5. Bump the version and update the date. Do not restate feature requirements — those belong in specs.

Output only the edited constitution. Be concise.

---
name: amby-converge
description: "Check the codebase against spec, plan, and tasks after implementing; append gap tasks, never edit code."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/converge.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Converge feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature): does the code satisfy its artifacts?
Never edit source code — only that feature's `tasks.md` and `spec.md` are writable.

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=converge` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.
Then run `ambykit trace <feature> --json`; if it fails, go on as without it. Its uncovered requirements are
gaps already — do not re-derive coverage by reading every test; read tests only to judge whether the covered
ones truly satisfy their requirement.

1. No `tasks.md` → stop, say to run `/amby.tasks`. No `plan.md` → converge on spec + tasks and say so.
2. For every `FR-###`/`SC-###`, plan decision (incl. `data-model.md`/`contracts/`), and checked
   `T###`: look for evidence only in files the plan/tasks name. Classify **covered**, **gap**
   (absent), or **unverified** (inconclusive). Skip items the plan marks deferred/out of scope. If `tests.md`
   exists, read it after the `trace` matrix (where there is one) and treat its cases as the expected tests; spend
   effort only on what neither answers.
3. **Append, don't rewrite.** Under `## Convergence` in `tasks.md` (create at the end if absent) add
   `- [ ] [T###] [US#] … (closes NNN:FR-###)` per gap and `- [ ] [T###] [US#] [VERIFY] …` per unverified
   item. Continue IDs from the highest `T###` anywhere in the file; skip items already listed
   unchecked there. Nothing to add → leave the file untouched.
4. In `spec.md`, change only statuses: a story → `done` (`ambykit edit status <feature> US-# done`) when every
   FR/SC it maps to is covered; the feature's frontmatter `status:` → `done` when all stories are.
5. Report: **converged** (no gaps) or **gaps found (N)**, counts per class, and a table of every ID
   with its class and a one-line reason for each gap/unverified item.
roles..github/skills/amby-decide/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-decide
description: "Record a decision as a numbered record — cited by ID, supersedable, checked by analyze."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/decide.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Record the decision in `${input:args}`. Callable from any phase; it has no role of its own.

If a current feature applies, run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=decide` first; ignore any error.

1. No decision text → ask for it in one question. Read `.amby/decisions/README.md` (the index) only;
   if a row's title already covers the decision, name that `ADR-###` and stop — do not duplicate.
2. Number: highest of the `ADR-###.md` files **and** the index rows, plus 1, three digits. Never reuse a
   number, even for a deleted file. Create `.amby/decisions/` and its index (`| ID | Title | Status |`)
   on first use.
3. Write `.amby/decisions/ADR-<n>.md` from `@.amby/templates/adr.md`: Context, Decision, Alternatives,
   Consequences, each short. Fill `feature` from the current feature and `principle` when relevant.
   The file name is the id, with no slug.
4. Principle conflict: if the decision conflicts with a constitution principle, set `status: proposed`,
   list the principle numbers in `conflicts`, and tell the person it needs their call. Never write
   `accepted` with `conflicts` filled. Otherwise `status: accepted`.
5. `--supersede ADR-###`: set `supersedes` on the new record, and on the old record set
   `status: superseded` and `superseded-by: <new id>`. Both sides, always. Never edit the old record's body.
6. A wording-only edit of an existing record keeps its `id` and `status`.
7. Patch the index in place: add or update this record's row. Leave rows of deleted files (tombstones).
8. Cite decisions elsewhere only by `ADR-###`; never restate them. End with the id and path.
roles..github/skills/amby-design/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-design
description: "Design the UI — wireframes, component specs, and design tokens — with a sign-off gate."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/design.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Design the UI for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read that feature's `spec.md`, the templates `@.amby/templates/ui.md` +
`@.amby/templates/design-tokens.json`, and — for detailed rules — `@.amby/reference/design-conventions.md`.
Design for the spec's user stories.

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=design` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. Write `ui.md` following the template: per story, a layout/wireframe (ASCII or embedded SVG), a
   component inventory (props + full state set + token names), interaction criteria in
   Given/When/Then tied to the `US-#`, and content/accessibility notes (WCAG AA).
2. Write/extend `design-tokens.json` in three tiers — primitive → semantic → component. In `ui.md`

3. Keep the UI consistent with any constitution UX principle (cite by number).

   box and set `signed_off: true` (with reviewer + date) in the frontmatter. Until then it's a draft.

---
name: amby-implement
description: "Execute the task list, checking off tasks and updating story status as you go."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/implement.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Act as the **Developer** in `@.amby/roles/developer.md` and say so in your first line. If `${input:args}` contains `--as <id>`, use `@.amby/roles/<id>.md` instead; if that file is missing, stop and list the files in `.amby/roles/`.

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=implement` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. From `tasks.md`, pick the target task(s). If `.amby/lane/lane.json` exists you are in a lane: work
   only the task ids it lists. Respect the Foundational-before-features gate and the
   story dependency graph — never start a task whose story is `blocked-by` unfinished work.
2. Load **only** the slice you need: the task line, the relevant `plan.md` section, and the specific
   files named. Don't read the whole spec tree (token-frugal).
3. Implement to satisfy the mapped `FR-###`/acceptance criteria and the constitution. Add/adjust
   tests for the acceptance criteria: build to the story's cases in `tests.md` and name tests `NNN:FR-###: …`;
   at the story checkpoint say if `tests.md` is missing, never pass silently. If you cannot finish a task, add `⚠ BLOCKED: <reason>` as the last
   segment of its line (after its `(file/path)` group, if it has one), stop that task and continue with another unblocked
   one; note any departure from the plan as `↪ DEVIATION: <note>`. Remove `⚠ BLOCKED:` once resolved.
4. **Patch in place:** flip the completed task's checkbox to `- [x]` in `tasks.md`; while a story is partway run
   `ambykit edit status <feature> US-# in-progress`. Never edit story data, files or Verify results by hand: use
   `ambykit edit status|files|verify`. After each checked task, run
   `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=implement --task=T###` (ignore errors).
5. At a phase checkpoint, run that phase's Verify check (its `**Verify:**` line or `verify:` block) before passing it
   (none: say so and continue). Record the result with
   `ambykit edit verify <feature> <phase> --result=passed|failed|unverified [--why=<why>]`, replacing any earlier one.
   Never pass the checkpoint on a failure: fix it and run again. If you cannot run the check, ask a person to run or
   confirm it and record `unverified`. Only once the Verify has passed (or there is none) and all of a story's tasks
   are done, run `ambykit edit status <feature> US-# done`. In a lane, record the result after the phase's lanes are merged.
6. Run `ambykit analyze` and fix any `file:line` error it reports for this feature. Report what you did and the next
   unblocked task. Stop at a story checkpoint for review.

Act as the **Architect** in `@.amby/roles/architect.md` and say so in your first line. If `${input:args}` contains `--as <id>`, use `@.amby/roles/<id>.md` instead; if that file is missing, stop and list the files in `.amby/roles/`.

Write the implementation plan for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read that feature's `spec.md` and `ui.md`, plus `@.amby/constitution.md`.

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=plan` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. Write `plan.md` following `@.amby/templates/plan.md`: technical context (stack, libraries,

2. This is the **first artifact with technology decisions.** Ensure every choice honors the

3. Map each `FR-###`/`US-#` to how the design satisfies it. **Reference by ID — do not restate the

roles..github/skills/amby-revise/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-revise
description: "Continue an existing feature's spec (or design) — add and refine in place, with a done-guard."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/revise.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Continue the spec (and, optionally, the design) for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read only that feature's `spec.md` (and its `ui.md` if continuing design) plus the structure
of `@.amby/templates/spec.md`. This command **extends** an existing feature — it is not `specify`
(which starts a new feature) nor `clarify` (which only resolves `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers).

2. **Done-guard.** If the `spec.md` frontmatter `status:` is `done`, make no edits: tell the author the
   feature is complete and to run `/amby.specify` for a new feature. Stop here.
3. Otherwise **continue in place** (patch, never regenerate — Principle 3):
   - Add new user stories (`US-#`), requirements (`FR-###`), and success criteria (`SC-###`), each
     taking the **next available number**. Preserve every existing id and its text verbatim. A new story
     also gets an entry (`id`, `priority`, `status`, dependencies) in the frontmatter `stories:` list of a
     v2 spec; change a story's status with `ambykit edit status <feature> US-# <status>`.
   - Refine existing items only where the author asked; keep their ids stable.
   - New requirements use EARS (SHALL / WHEN / WHILE / IF-THEN / WHERE); new acceptance criteria use
     Given/When/Then — consistent with `specify`.
   - Leave any story already marked `status: done` untouched; you may still add new stories.
   - If `tests.md` exists, mark each case citing a changed criterion `[stale]` and each citing a removed one
     `[obsolete]` (never delete); change nothing else there.
4. Set the `spec.md` frontmatter `status:` to `in-progress`.
5. **Design (optional).** If the author is continuing the UI/design and `ui.md` exists, extend it in
   place, preserving existing sections. If `ui.md` does **not** exist, do not create it here — direct
   the author to run `/amby.design`.
6. Keep edits minimal and token-frugal; cite the constitution by principle number where relevant.

Run `ambykit analyze` and fix any `file:line` error it reports for this spec. Report what you added or
changed, by id.
roles..github/skills/amby-run/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-run
description: "Run a feature's tasks as a team — workers build, QA and architect review, state kept in files, resumable."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/run.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Run the feature in `${input:args}` (number or name; `--new` only when the person asked for a new run). You are the
**lead**: you start workers, hand out task IDs, run the reviews and keep the run state. You have no role of
your own. Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=run` first; ignore any error.

Subagents on this host: `no`. If `yes`, workers are the `amby-worker` subagent and reviewers the
`amby-qa` and `amby-architect` subagents (roles `@.amby/roles/qa.md`, `@.amby/roles/architect.md`). If `no`,
say so once, then do each worker, QA and architect step yourself, in sequence, one task at a time, with the
same commands and state files below: claim, edit, check off, report; QA before architect, each acting as its
role file, and say which role you are acting as.

Every step works from files with these verbs alone, and nothing here needs a server: `ambykit fleet`,
`ambykit activity`, `ambykit directive`.

## 1. Resume or start

Run `ambykit fleet status <feature>`; it prints the run, the next phase, lanes, free slots and warnings.

- **Done** → say so and change nothing. **Stopped** naming `spec.md`, `plan.md` or `tasks.md` (missing, or the
  spec still `draft`) → stop, name that artifact and the command that makes it.
- **No unfinished run** → `ambykit fleet start <feature>` (this invocation is the request; `--new` starts another
  run on request only). **One** → resume it. **Several** → list them and ask which; never pick.
- **Warning: state missing or corrupt** → `ambykit fleet status <feature> --run=<id> --rebuild`, then go on.
  Checked tasks in `tasks.md` stay checked, so nothing completed is repeated.
- Load by reference only: the current phase of `@specs/<feature>/tasks.md`, the plan sections and `US-#`/`FR-###`
  its tasks cite, and `@specs/<feature>/tests.md` when it exists. Never whole artifacts.

## 2. Work the phase (stage `working`)

- Take the phase's open, unblocked tasks from `status`. Tasks are independent when their file ownership is
  disjoint. If two tasks you want to run together own overlapping files, see **Overlap**.
- **Caps:** `status` shows free slots (default 3 workers, 2 per assistant type). Never start a worker without one.
- Per worker: `ambykit fleet update <feature> --worker-start=<lane> --assistant=<id> --tasks=T001,T002`
  (`<lane>` is `lane-<phase>-<k>`, `<id>` the assistant the worker runs on, the same id as your `--agent`; it is refused
  when no slot is free). Give the worker only: the feature, run,
  lane, its task IDs, their file ownership and the artifacts by `@path`. It returns one line per task.
- Workers report on a fixed rule, which you must also keep. Report at the start of a task, at the end of a task, and whenever you are blocked or waiting. Never report on a timer and never report progress.
- When a worker finishes: `ambykit fleet update <feature> --worker-done=<lane>`.
- **Blocked:** the worker marks the task `⚠ BLOCKED: <reason>` and you continue with other unblocked tasks.
  Blocked work is yours to resolve or give to the person; workers never ask each other.
- **Stalled:** `status` flags a lane with no report and no `tasks.md` change for the stall limit. Restart it with
  `ambykit fleet update <feature> --restart=<lane>` and re-delegate its unchecked IDs. After the restart limit the
  command pauses the lane and asks for a person: only they may approve moving it to another assistant or marking
  its task BLOCKED.
- **Notes and claims:** workers claim files before editing (`ambykit fleet claim`), post one-line notes
  (`ambykit fleet note`) and their claims are released when a task is checked off. A refused claim names the
  owner; sort it out through the board and `status` warnings, not by editing the file.

## 3. QA (stage `qa`)

When every task of the phase is checked: `ambykit fleet update <feature> --stage=qa`. Ask QA (`@.amby/roles/qa.md`, read-only) to:

1. run the phase's Verify check (its `**Verify:**` line, or the `verify:` block of a v2 file), and check the acceptance
   criteria of its stories; if `tests.md` exists, its cases for these tasks are the expected tests. No Verify check →
   check the criteria only and say the phase has none.
2. return a verdict. You write it to `.amby/fleet/<run>/verdicts/<lane>.qa.<round>.json`
   (`<round>` = failed rounds so far + 1): `{"verdict":"pass"|"fail","findings":[{"id","severity","finding","fix"}]}`.
3. record the result with `ambykit edit verify <feature> <phase> --result=passed|failed|unverified [--why=<why>]` (the file
   shows `✓ passed`, `✗ failed: <why>` or `? unverified`); when the check cannot be run here, tell the person, ask them to
   confirm and record `unverified`. Set a finished story with `ambykit edit status <feature> US-# done`; never edit a
   `files:`/`verify:` block or story data by hand.

A failing Verify never passes the checkpoint. Do not tick the checkpoint or start the next phase until it passes.

## 4. Architect review (stage `architect`)

After QA passes: `ambykit fleet update <feature> --stage=architect`. Ask the architect (`@.amby/roles/architect.md`, read-only) for correctness,
simplification and fit with `plan.md`; findings by stable ID, same verdict file with `.architect.`.

- **Fail** (QA or architect): `ambykit fleet update <feature> --round=<failed rounds so far>`. It prints `retry` or
  `escalate`. **retry** → return only the finding IDs and their `fix` to the **same worker** (same lane) and go back
  to `working`. **escalate** (the round limit) → stop: summarize the open findings and ask the person to decide.
  Record their answer with `ambykit fleet update <feature> --decision="<text>"` and continue from it.
- **Pass:** `ambykit fleet update <feature> --phase=<next>`; after the last phase,
  `ambykit fleet update <feature> --done`, then suggest `/amby.converge`.

## Pause, resume, stop

When the person asks: `ambykit fleet update <feature> --pause` (or `--resume`, `--stop`; add `=<lane>` for one lane).
This writes a directive per lane; start no new worker while paused. The directive protocol is: The reply carries a directive: continue, pause or stop. On pause or stop, finish the task you are on, then obey it at your next report: do not start another task.
The run state records `paused`; the next `/amby.run` resumes from it.

## Overlap

If workers' files overlap, choose before any work starts and record it:
- **Serialize:** one worker after the other. `ambykit fleet update <feature> --overlap=serialized --lanes=a,b --order=a,b`
- **Squad:** one writer per shared file, a fixed merge order; others send change requests through the writer or you.
  `ambykit fleet update <feature> --overlap=squad --lanes=a,b --shared=<path>,... --writer=<path>:<lane>,... --order=a,b`

## Rules

- All review roles, including `security`, stay read-only; never give them write access. Only workers write code.
- Keep every status line to one line; no logs, no restated artifacts.

---
name: amby-specify
description: "Turn a feature idea into a spec — user stories, EARS requirements, acceptance criteria."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/specify.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Write a specification for: **${input:args}**

Context: read `@.amby/constitution.md` and the structure of `@.amby/templates/spec.md` only. Do not
read other specs.

1. Create the feature dir `specs/NNN-slug/` (next number, kebab-slug from the title) and write
   `spec.md` following `@.amby/templates/spec.md`. Then run
   `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=specify` with the new number; ignore any error.
2. Define **user stories** (`US-#`): role / capability / benefit, why that priority, and an
   independent-test statement. Put each story's `priority` (P1/P2/P3), `status: draft` and
   `depends-on`/`blocked-by` in the frontmatter `stories:` list; the heading carries the title only.
3. Write **acceptance criteria** in Given/When/Then per story.
4. Write **functional requirements** (`FR-###`) in EARS notation (SHALL / WHEN / WHILE / IF-THEN /
   WHERE). Each must be testable.
5. Write measurable, tech-agnostic **success criteria** (`SC-###`).
6. **Capture WHAT/WHY only — no technology choices.** Flag every unknown inline as
   `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: …]` instead of guessing.
7. If `.amby/config.json` has `"worktrees": true` and this is a git repo, run
   `ambykit worktree NNN-slug` (the only command to run) and tell the user to continue in
   `.worktrees/NNN-slug/`. Otherwise skip this step (say why if isolation was enabled but git is absent).

Keep it tight. Reference the constitution by principle number where relevant; don't restate it. Then run
`ambykit analyze` and fix any `file:line` error it reports for this spec.
roles..github/skills/amby-tasks/SKILL.md:
---
name: amby-tasks
description: "Break the plan into an ordered, dependency-aware task checklist."
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/tasks.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Generate `tasks.md` for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read that feature's `plan.md` (and `spec.md` for story IDs/priorities/dependencies).

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot-cli --phase=tasks` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. Write tasks in the v2 form of `@.amby/templates/tasks.md` (even if `spec.md` is 1.x): checkbox lines
   `- [ ] [T###] [P?] [US#] description`, then each phase's `yaml` block.
2. Group into phases: **Setup → Foundational → User stories (by priority) → Polish**. Enforce the
   gate: no user-story task before Foundational completes.
3. Order tasks by the story **dependency graph** (`depends-on`/`blocked-by`) and priority. Mark
   independent tasks `[P]`. Tag each task with its `[US#]`. End each story group with a checkpoint.
4. Give every task a stable `T###` id and list its files in its phase's `files:` block, never on the task
   line: repo-relative, dirs end `/`, no globs. Mark `[P]` only when no other task in the same phase shares or
   nests a path.
5. End every phase with exactly ONE `verify:` in its block, whose `check:` is a runnable check or observable
   condition that proves the phase works (e.g. a test command). Never more than one.
6. Also write `tests.md` (the test design) in this phase per `@.amby/templates/tests.md`, touching only `tasks.md`
   and `tests.md`. If `spec.md` is not `status: ready`, skip it and say the spec must be ready first. One case per
   acceptance criterion (negative and edge ones too, max 15 per story); one too vague to test goes under `## Flags`.
   With `--skip-tests <reason>`, write `tests.md` holding only the line `skipped: <reason>`.
7. Cases are `auto` unless a fixed-list reason makes them manual (add `verify:` and `record:`). Each cites its `US-n#k`
   and `FR-###`s; `TC-###` is highest + 1, never reused. An FR with no case goes under `## Uncovered` with a reason.
   With an existing `tests.md`, patch only the cases citing changed criteria (keep their ids, clear `[stale]`), mark
   cases whose criterion was removed `[obsolete]` and add new ones; leave the rest untouched.

Do not start implementing. Keep descriptions to one line each. Then run `ambykit analyze` and fix any
`file:line` error it reports for this feature.

# AGENTS.md — demo

### AmbyKit usage

This project uses **AmbyKit** for Spec-Driven Development. Build features by producing structured
artifacts before code: a constitution, specs (user stories + EARS requirements), UI design, a plan,
and an ordered task list.

**Workflow commands**

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/amby.constitution` | Create or amend the project constitution — durable, cross-feature principles. |
| `/amby.specify` | Turn a feature idea into a spec — user stories, EARS requirements, acceptance criteria. |
| `/amby.clarify` | Resolve the open [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers in a feature spec. |
| `/amby.revise` | Continue an existing feature's spec (or design) — add and refine in place, with a done-guard. |
| `/amby.design` | Design the UI — wireframes, component specs, and design tokens — with a sign-off gate. |
| `/amby.plan` | Produce the technical implementation plan (the HOW) from an approved spec and UI. |
| `/amby.tasks` | Break the plan into an ordered, dependency-aware task checklist. |
| `/amby.analyze` | Cross-check spec, plan, and tasks for coverage, consistency, and dependency-graph health. |
| `/amby.implement` | Execute the task list, checking off tasks and updating story status as you go. |
| `/amby.converge` | Check the codebase against spec, plan, and tasks after implementing; append gap tasks, never edit code. |
| `/amby.review` | Review an artifact from another role's perspective — findings by stable ID, advisory only. |
| `/amby.decide` | Record a decision as a numbered record — cited by ID, supersedable, checked by analyze. |
| `/amby.run` | Run a feature's tasks as a team — workers build, QA and architect review, state kept in files, resumable. |

**Rules for agents**

- Read `.amby/constitution.md` and honor its principles in every phase.
- Specs (`specs/NNN-*/spec.md`) capture WHAT/WHY with **no technology choices**; plans capture HOW.
- Requirements use EARS (WHEN/WHILE/IF…THE SYSTEM SHALL…) with Given/When/Then acceptance criteria.
- Reference artifacts by stable id (US-#, FR-###, SC-###); don't restate them. Patch in place.
- Task checkboxes in `tasks.md` are the source of truth for progress (`ambykit dashboard`).
- Decisions live in `.amby/decisions/` (`/amby.decide`). Cite them as `ADR-###`; load only the cited records plus the index.
- **Current feature** (when a phase gets no id): the enclosing `.worktrees/NNN-slug/` directory (or a
  lane, `.worktrees/NNN-slug.lane-P-K/`, which belongs to `NNN-slug`) if the project root is one; else the git branch, if it names a `specs/` dir; else the highest-numbered
  `specs/` dir — say which you chose. `ambykit worktree <id>` gives a feature its own working copy.
